html:
SMTO-GWT-0044 — A running AI model is stopping this Gateway from restarting

GUID: 7ca912a9-4679-4dd2-9812-15288aa954bb
Slug: gateway-restart-llm-running
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • SMTO tried to restart the Gateway on this computer, but an AI model the Gateway manages is still running there. To avoid cutting that model off, the Gateway did not restart.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO in a conversation to stop the local AI model running on that computer, and approve the action when SMTO asks. Stopping the model interrupts any answer it is writing, and the Gateway won't restart while a model it manages is still running.
  2. Ask SMTO to show the model's status on that computer, and wait until it says the model has stopped. A model that is still shutting down, or whose state is unclear, still blocks the restart.
  3. Then repeat the restart the same way you started it. If you use the /restart command, remember it restarts SMTO and all its Gateways, even while Tasks are running. A fresh restart request is checked against the model's current state, and knowing what /restart affects avoids interrupting other work.

What success looks like

  • The restart goes ahead and the computer shows Connected again in Settings › Setup › Gateways.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that computer's Gateway. Don't end the model's process by hand on that computer; ask the manager to stop it properly.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GatewayService refused the restart (409) because a Gateway-managed model process is still running (the legacy LLM runtime, or a local AI runtime that is live or in an unknown state).

What this means

  • Gateway restart found a live process owned by the local AI runtime manager and refused to terminate the Gateway around that process. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway restart found a live process owned by the local AI runtime manager and refused to terminate the Gateway around that process.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owned local AI runtime list and distinguish it from unrelated model processes on the host.

How to fix it

  • Stop the managed model first: POST /llm/stop for the legacy runtime, or the Local AI stop operation for each live runtime (a runtime in unknown state also blocks restart). Wait until its status confirms it has stopped, then issue a fresh restart request. Gateway updates through Software updates stop managed models themselves.
  • Use the managed model Stop action, wait for confirmed termination, and then request the Gateway restart.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The owning runtime reports confirmed termination, after which the Gateway admits restart.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
